title: US stock rally falters near record as oil fluctuates
article:
(Sept 23): A sense of caution prevailed on Wall Street after a rally that put stocks on the verge of their all-time highs, with oil prices wavering as traders looked for signs of diplomatic efforts to revive the Strait of Hormuz.

The S&P 500 was little changed. A closely watched gauge of chipmakers climbed for a sixth straight day, poised for the longest winning streak since April. A measure of big banks lost 2.2%. Brent crude hovered near US$100. Treasury yields edged up ahead of a US$69 billion sale of two-year notes. The dollar rose.

President Donald Trump said he believes the US will make a deal with Iran after the election, adding that more oil is flowing than at any point since the war started while noting prices will plummet when the conflict is over. He addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

“What happens this week may become critical for the direction of crude oil prices over the medium term,” said Thierry Wizman at Macquarie Group. “That’s because the key actors in the US-Iran war will be having meetings in New York.”

Any agreements that come out of those discussions may determine whether the conflict continues and intensifies or whether an off-ramp is found, he added.

After his speech on Tuesday, Trump was due to meet Gulf state leaders, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, before later hosting a reception for other leaders and sitting down with Venezuela’s Delcy Rodriguez.

He’s set to return to Washington late on Tuesday, ahead of a visit by China’s Xi Jinping.

Traders also kept a close eye on the latest remarks from central bank officials.

Federal Reserve Bank of Boston president Susan Collins said she supported last week’s decision to raise interest rates, which she said would help bring inflation back to the 2% target.

Her New York counterpart John Williams noted the shift to central clearing for US Treasuries and Treasury-collateralised repurchase agreements was ahead of schedule.

“Leadership has rotated decisively back towards semiconductors and hyperscalers, giving the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 enough to keep pushing higher without signs of an outright upside chase, but a more convincing rally requires broader participation,” says Michael Ball, Macro Strategist, Markets Live at Bloomberg strategists.

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The S&P 500 was little changed as of 12.02pm New York time
• The MSCI World Index was little changed
